data.name: Groot OS — Real-Time Voice-Reactive AI Interface
data.description: End-to-end sub-1.5s speech-to-speech AI platform combining a React/Vite live waveform UI with a FastAPI WebSocket audio pipeline, Groq Whisper v3-turbo, TF-IDF RAG memory, multi-LLM failover across 10+ models, and streaming Edge-TTS.

caseStudy.overview: Groot OS is a production-deployed, full-duplex conversational voice AI assistant built to deliver natural, human-paced voice interaction in under 1.5 seconds. Instead of blocking on sequential HTTP calls, it streams audio over WebSockets, retrieves relevant context via lightweight TF-IDF + cosine-similarity RAG, routes inference across 10+ LLMs with automatic failover, and chunks neural TTS at sentence boundaries with instant user barge-in.
caseStudy.problem: Most web-based voice AI demos suffer from 4–7 second dead-air delays because they wait for the entire LLM response to finish before synthesizing speech, crash when a single free-tier model hits a 429 rate limit, and cannot be interrupted mid-sentence.
capabilities: Sub-1.5s full-duplex speech-to-speech pipeline using Groq Whisper (whisper-large-v3-turbo) and streaming neural Edge-TTS.
Dynamic Multi-LLM Failover Router across 10+ OpenRouter and Groq models with automatic circuit-breaking on timeouts or rate limits.
Lightweight local RAG memory engine built with Scikit-learn TF-IDF vectorization and cosine similarity for zero-latency context injection.
Interactive React/Vite voice HUD featuring real-time audio waveform rendering and instant barge-in interruption.
architecture: Client Audio Capture (React/Vite + Web Audio API): Streams user voice frames over a persistent WebSocket while visualizing microphone amplitude and managing an ordered audio playback queue.
Ingestion & Transcription (FastAPI + Groq Whisper v3-turbo): Receives raw audio buffers asynchronously and transcribes speech in ~200–300ms.
Context & Routing Layer: Queries Scikit-learn TF-IDF + cosine similarity memory for relevant past facts, then dispatches the prompt to a priority-ordered OpenRouter/Groq LLM router.
Sentence-Boundary TTS Chunking: As tokens stream in, the backend flushes complete sentences directly to Edge-TTS and pushes MP3 audio chunks down the WebSocket before generation even finishes.
challenges: Eliminated mid-sentence audio stutter by decoupling TTS synthesis from WebSocket frame emission via an async producer-consumer queue.
Implemented deterministic barge-in handling: when the user speaks during playback, the client immediately flushes queued Web Audio buffers and signals the FastAPI task to cancel in-flight generation.
Replaced heavy vector-database roundtrips with in-memory Scikit-learn TF-IDF retrieval, cutting RAG overhead to single-digit milliseconds.
caseStudy.takeaway: Demonstrates production readiness in asynchronous Python (FastAPI, WebSockets), real-time browser audio APIs, fault-tolerant LLM routing, and low-latency system optimization—skills directly transferable to AI product teams and real-time backend engineering roles.

data.name: InLine — Real-Time Collaborative Code Editor
data.description: Full-duplex collaborative coding workspace (Google Docs for developers) built with a React/TypeScript CodeMirror 6 frontend and a distributed Node.js + Express + Socket.io room synchronization backend delivering sub-20ms multi-cursor sync.

caseStudy.overview: InLine (CodeSync) is a zero-setup collaborative web IDE built for live technical interviews, pair programming, and remote debugging. It pairs a TypeScript + React + CodeMirror 6 workspace with a Node.js + Express + Socket.io synchronization server to broadcast edits and multi-user cursor positions across rooms in under 20ms.

highlights.label: Modular TypeScript editor with syntax themes

caseStudy.problem: Screen-sharing code over video calls introduces compression blur and forces one developer to type while others watch passively. Engineering teams and interviewers need an instant, shareable URL where multiple peers can edit and navigate the same buffer concurrently.
capabilities: Instant shareable coding rooms with isolated WebSocket namespaces and live participant presence indicators.
Real-time multi-user cursor tracking and document synchronization across distributed browser tabs.
CodeMirror 6 editor integration with multi-language syntax highlighting, TailwindCSS UI, and AI-assisted code completions.
architecture: Frontend Workspace (React + TypeScript + Vite + TailwindCSS): Hosts the CodeMirror 6 editor instance, room join/share controls, language switcher, and AI completion panel.
WebSocket Transport (Node.js + Express + Socket.io): Maintains active room memberships, broadcasts incremental document changes to peer sockets, and relays cursor/selection offsets.
Conflict & Loop Prevention: Tags remote state updates with origin annotations before dispatching editor transactions so incoming changes never re-trigger outbound socket emissions.
challenges: Eliminated infinite edit echo loops between local `onChange` listeners and incoming Socket.io updates by tagging remote transactions at the CodeMirror 6 state layer.
Handled abrupt tab closures and network reconnects gracefully so room participant lists and remote cursor decorations stay accurate without memory leaks.
caseStudy.takeaway: Proves strong full-stack TypeScript fundamentals, stateful WebSocket architecture, and event-driven UI engineering—core capabilities sought by SaaS, developer-tooling, and collaborative web product teams.

data.name: CodeGraph — Interactive AST Visualizer
data.description: AI-powered developer tool built with Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, React Flow, and Supabase (PostgreSQL) that recursively maps GitHub repository ASTs and ES module imports into interactive dependency graphs with animated path tracing.

caseStudy.overview: CodeGraph accelerates codebase onboarding by turning any public GitHub repository into an interactive, zoomable dependency graph. Built on Next.js 15 App Router and TypeScript, it recursively parses ASTs and ES module imports, visualizes relationships with animated React Flow edges, and caches parsed graphs in Supabase PostgreSQL for instant repeat loads.
caseStudy.problem: Onboarding onto a new repository usually requires opening dozens of files just to trace which modules import what. Standard GitHub file trees show folder nesting, not actual architectural coupling or dependency chains.
capabilities: One-click GitHub URL ingestion that fetches repository trees and recursively resolves ES import/export graphs.
Interactive React Flow canvas with pan/zoom, animated dependency path highlighting, and node-level AI architectural summaries via OpenRouter.
Persistent Supabase PostgreSQL caching layer so previously analyzed repositories render instantaneously without burning GitHub API quota.
architecture: Ingestion & AST Engine (Next.js Server Layer): Fetches repository trees via GitHub REST APIs, filters source modules, and extracts static import/export edges.
Path Resolution Normalizer: Maps relative imports (`./`, `../`, `@/` aliases, and `index.ts` barrels) onto canonical file paths so graph edges connect cleanly.
Visualization & Caching (React Flow + Supabase): Stores computed node/edge JSON in PostgreSQL and renders interactive directed graphs with TailwindCSS v4.
challenges: Solved edge-case relative import and barrel-file (`index.ts`) resolution across deeply nested TypeScript monorepos without false orphan nodes.
Bypassed GitHub unauthenticated rate-limit bottlenecks by persisting parsed dependency graphs in Supabase PostgreSQL keyed by repository commit state.
caseStudy.takeaway: Showcases strong Next.js 15 + TypeScript full-stack ownership, compiler/AST fundamentals, PostgreSQL caching design, and polished data visualization—ideal for developer-experience and product engineering internships.

data.name: Arclane — Autonomous SMB Website Builder & Growth Engine
data.description: Production v3.3.1 producer-consumer automation ecosystem that discovers Indian SMBs lacking a web presence, runs a 14-point AI strategic audit, automatically generates and deploys bespoke responsive websites to GitHub & Vercel, and orchestrates outreach via Telegram HUD, Local Web UI, and WhatsApp.

caseStudy.overview: Arclane is an end-to-end, 24/7 autonomous business growth and web-generation platform built for Indian SMBs (clinics, gyms, salons, cafes). Using a Producer-Consumer streaming IPC architecture, it discovers local businesses without modern websites, crawls their social/web footprint for a 14-point AI audit, automatically builds and deploys bespoke responsive Tailwind/Next.js websites to GitHub and Vercel, updates a Google Sheets CRM, and coordinates outreach through a dual Telegram Bot + Local Web UI control plane.

highlights.label: Programmatic Tailwind/Next.js site generation & Vercel deploy
Deep web & social crawler + LLM strategic scoring
Telegram Controller Bot + Local Web UI (:3000)

caseStudy.problem: Millions of Indian SMBs rely solely on Google Maps listings without a fast, mobile-friendly website, while traditional agencies spend hours manually prospecting, auditing, designing preview sites, and tracking follow-ups in spreadsheets.
capabilities: Automated Bespoke Website Builder & Vercel Deployer: Generates tailored, responsive Tailwind CSS / Next.js websites per business, creates/syncs GitHub repositories, and deploys live preview URLs directly to Vercel.
Producer-Consumer IPC Streaming Pipeline: Emits structured `[STREAM_LEAD]` JSON events over `stdout` from Playwright workers straight into the BI & website-generation consumer.
Deep Business Intelligence Engine: Crawls existing links/socials and runs a 14-point AI audit (Gemini Flash Lite + OpenRouter) to customize site copy and value propositions.
Dual Control Plane & CRM Sync: Synchronizes live pipeline states with Google Sheets CRM and lets operators monitor, pause, or trigger waves via Telegram Bot commands or the Local Web UI.
architecture: 1. Discovery & Watchdog (`scraper/`): Playwright engine executes bounded micro-locality grid hopping with multi-source phone extraction (`wa.me`, `tel:`, DOM regex) and `scraped_places.txt` deduplication.
2. Stream Runner & Controller (`controller_bot/`): Consumes `[STREAM_LEAD]` IPC events and manages `Asia/Kolkata` cron schedules for staggered outreach waves and deal-closing call scripts.

3. Deep BI & Automated Website Builder (`src/` + `web-dev-agency`): Runs the 14-point LLM audit, compiles custom responsive Tailwind/Next.js landing pages, pushes to GitHub, and triggers Vercel production deployments.
4. Multi-Channel Dispatch & CRM: Logs live deployed preview URLs back into Google Sheets and dispatches staggered WhatsApp Web / email notifications with human-like 30–75s delays.
challenges: Eliminated long-running Chromium memory leaks by architecting `run_forever.py` to process 50-lead chunks and cleanly recycle browser processes, backed by a watchdog that auto-restarts deadlocked sessions after 3 minutes.
Built boundary exhaustion safeguards and persistent state checkpoints so 12-hour autopilot runs never duplicate businesses or lose progress on restart.
Enforced dual-repo Git synchronization (`auto_commit.js`) and strict secret hygiene across both the core engine and the nested `web-dev-agency` deployment repo.
caseStudy.takeaway: Demonstrates rare end-to-end systems engineering: building resilient 24/7 worker daemons, IPC streaming pipelines, automated CI/CD website generation via GitHub/Vercel APIs, and production observability—ideal for backend, automation, and full-stack product internships.

data.name: Wearable AI Reading & Multimodal Study Assistant
data.description: Hands-free Kotlin Android accessibility and study device pairing Camera2 API live capture, Bluetooth foot-pedal hardware HID navigation, Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite multimodal reasoning, and native Text-to-Speech narration.

caseStudy.overview: A hands-free wearable reading and study assistant written in Kotlin for Android. By combining hardware Bluetooth foot-pedal controls with the Android Camera2 API, Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite vision reasoning, and native Text-to-Speech, it enables students and visually impaired users to scan, understand, and listen to printed textbooks or problem sets without touching a phone screen.
caseStudy.problem: Touch-based OCR mobile apps force users to hold a phone steady, tap small capture buttons, and scroll through dense text—making them unusable for hands-busy desk study or users with visual/motor impairments.
capabilities: Physical Bluetooth foot-pedal event bus allowing eyes-free page capture, section navigation, and audio replay.
High-clarity image capture via Android Camera2 API streamed directly to Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite for OCR and step-by-step explanations.
Speech-friendly audio narration via Android's native Text-to-Speech engine.
architecture: Hardware Input Layer (Kotlin HID Listener): Intercepts Bluetooth foot-pedal key events and maps single/double-press gestures to capture, pause, and repeat commands.
Vision Capture Pipeline (Camera2): Focuses and snaps high-resolution document frames on pedal trigger without requiring screen interaction.
Multimodal Reasoning & Audio Output: Sends image payloads to Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite with speech-optimized prompting, then streams the response into Android TTS.
challenges: Debounced hardware foot-pedal key events in Kotlin to eliminate accidental double-triggers during rapid page turns.
Engineered TTS-safe prompt instructions for Gemini Flash-Lite so equations and lists are spoken naturally instead of reading raw markdown symbols aloud.
caseStudy.takeaway: Shows versatility beyond web apps—native Kotlin/Android development, hardware HID integration, and human-centered accessibility engineering.

data.name: Robot — Local-First Humanoid Robot Intelligence Engine
data.description: Local-first humanoid robot AI engine combining Python asyncio, WebRTC AEC/NS, Silero VAD (<200ms barge-in), Piper ONNX TTS, llama.cpp (Qwen3.5-4B), YOLOv8 + YuNet 60 FPS spatial vision, WebGL2/Three.js 3D avatar, and a dual-column custom API router.

caseStudy.overview: Robot Core is a local-first humanoid intelligence engine engineered to run real-time speech, spatial computer vision, and 3D avatar rendering on edge hardware. It pairs a Python asyncio + FastAPI core (Silero VAD, WebRTC echo cancellation, llama.cpp Qwen3.5-4B, Piper ONNX TTS, and 60 FPS YOLOv8/YuNet vision) with a WebGL2/Three.js frontend and a hot-swappable Dual-Column Custom LLM API.
caseStudy.problem: Cloud-only robotics prototypes break whenever Wi-Fi drops, suffer from speaker-to-mic acoustic feedback loops, and lock hardware teams into a single LLM vendor.
capabilities: Local-first conversational pipeline with WebRTC Acoustic Echo Cancellation (AEC), Noise Suppression (NS), Silero VAD, and offline Piper ONNX TTS.
60 FPS real-time face detection and spatial object tracking powered by OpenCV, YuNet, and YOLOv8.
WebGL2 / Three.js 3D humanoid avatar synchronized with assistant speech states and personalities.
Dual-Column Custom API supporting hot-swappable OpenRouter and custom OpenAI-compatible inference providers alongside a Next.js Edge TTS proxy.
architecture: Audio & Barge-In Loop (Python asyncio): WebRTC AEC/NS cleans microphone input from speaker bleed, allowing Silero VAD to trigger <200ms barge-in interruptions.
Local + Cloud Dual Inference: Runs Qwen3.5-4B locally via `llama.cpp` or routes seamlessly through the FastAPI Dual-Column Custom API (OpenRouter / custom endpoints).
Spatial Vision Pipeline: Processes camera feeds at 60 FPS using YuNet face landmarks and YOLOv8 object detection.
Frontend & Voice Edge Route (Next.js + Three.js): Renders the interactive WebGL2 avatar and provides an Edge Runtime TTS synthesis endpoint.
challenges: Prevented the robot from hearing and transcribing its own voice by integrating WebRTC AEC/NS ahead of Silero VAD.
Built deterministic pytest unit tests with mocked engine fixtures to validate dual-provider config persistence and API updates safely.
Hardened repository security by parameterizing client tokens and scrubbing historical OAuth cache files across Git history.
caseStudy.takeaway: Demonstrates deep systems-level AI engineering—combining edge inference (`llama.cpp`, ONNX), real-time computer vision (YOLOv8 at 60 FPS), DSP audio hygiene (WebRTC AEC), and tested FastAPI + Next.js integration.
